newsitem.title: UK: BP leads oil stocks higher on rising crude.
newsitem.headline: BP leads oil stocks higher on rising crude.

text.p: Shares in Britain's leading oil stocks led the broader London market higher in pre-market trade on Tuesday tracking higher crude oil prices and ahead of BP's second quarter results.

Shares in BP were indicated 12-1/2p higher at 834-1/2p by 0725 GMT. Meanwhile, Shell gained 8p to 452-1/2p, Enterprise was up 7-1/2p at 709-1/2p, Burmah Castrol put on 19p to 10.62-1/2 and Lasmo was up 5p at 283-1/2p.

IPE September Brent crude oil ended up half a dollar at $19.45 a barrel on Monday after news that Occidental Petroleum had shut production and declared force majeure in the Colombian Cano Limon crude field.
The shutdown was the second in three weeks and it offset news of U.N. approval of an Iraqi aid distribution plan which removed the last obstacle for the resumption of crude oil exports by Baghdad.
Oil stocks climbed on the back of strength in the ADRs in the U.S., dealers said.
But BP later trimmed its gains on nervousness ahead of the company's second quarter earnings, due around 1000 GMT.
BP's replacement cost net income was forecast to rise to 661 million stg from 587 million stg the previous year.
